title: Publish guides, glossary and an inclusive onboarding hub
interface: Versioned resources/glossary and onboarding_progress use owner/review dates, visibility, checklist version and stable term aliases.
steps: Build Start Here checklist, contextual acronym explanations, service/process guides, who's-who links and practice sandbox task/request.
Provide head/publisher authoring with drafts, safe content, review reminders, ownership and published version. Treat MEA expansion as unconfirmed until supplied.
Allow skipped optional tours, late joiners and incomplete-task empty states; all core backgrounds receive equal guidance.
checks: A member with no affiliation/course disclosure can complete essential onboarding.
Renamed glossary label retains old alias and links without breaking forms.
Restricted resource/file does not become public through guide links or preview; sandbox never submits a real FIN case.

title: Manage roster, deployments, unit rename/merge/archive
interface: Organization commands preview impact, preserve UUID/history, reassign active work explicitly and create aliases; deployments are scoped dated grants.
steps: Build add/edit/archive unit and roster/deployment screens with active owners and service contacts. Avoid hardcoding the illustrative eight committees.
Implement rename/merge impact preview including open work, active reviewers and access deltas; old records preserve original unit identity.
Require replacement for orphaned active ownership/approval; merge does not silently union all privileges or move restricted case contents.
checks: Renaming MCD/unit keeps original tracking IDs and deep links.
Merge cannot unexpectedly grant another committee access to FIN/PRISM or historical private tasks.
Archiving a head/unit with active cases either assigns an authorized replacement or leaves explicit blocked work.

title: Build safe role editing and access explanations
interface: Role administration chooses fixed resource/action/scope capabilities, dated assignments and delegation ceilings; preview explains effective access without real impersonation.
steps: Build roles/permission grid, unit/record scope assignment, expiry, revoke and audit history for authorized grantors.
Protect last super admin, sensitive-review capabilities, emergency access boundary and no self-escalation; distinguish app roles from provider-console ownership.
Provide synthetic role preview and access-explanation results with current grants/mandatory constraints; no administrative read-all endpoint.
checks: Delegated head cannot grant FIN/PRISM/admin beyond grantor ceiling or edit own privileges upward.
Last technical custodian cannot be removed without a verified replacement path.
Membership/role expiry is honored immediately; synthetic preview cannot expose another user's real sensitive record.

title: Repair everyday workflows and implement shared configuration publication
interface: publish_configuration(expectedVersion, idempotencyKey) creates immutable version; rollback creates a new version and revalidates privilege/invariants.
steps: Establish supported configuration kinds and draft storage, version history, diff, validation, synthetic preview and explicit publish.
Validate same-term references, capability ceilings, reserved semantics and required gates before activation; preserve pinned historical requests.
Add conflict handling for simultaneous editors and canonical audit/outbox publication. No arbitrary JSON console bypass for business users.
checks: Invalid/missing references or removed mandatory FIN/MCD gate cannot publish.
Two administrators cannot overwrite each other's published version silently.
Rollback preserves intervening history and never rewrites open cases' pinned workflow/schema.

work: Batch35-R1, before new configuration screens: simplify the existing Overview, deliverable/task detail, request status and Resources entry paths. Show a specific permitted next action/owner/date/blocker first; open editing deliberately, group files/activity/verification separately, and reconcile Not required versus Pending versus Unavailable across readiness and FIN/MCD panels. Explain routine actions in plain language; retain applicable warnings and immutable evidence. Use existing src/features/{overview,deliverables,tasks,requests,resources,files} and scoped gate APIs; change a projection only if needed to carry authorized applicability, never infer permission from a hidden panel.

Batch35-R2: repair safe in-memory edit preservation or explicit discard confirmation across refresh/conflict/uncertain retry; retain idempotency and account/scope clearing. Restore one coherent synthetic member/head/guest first-work preview using existing components, with tasks gateway enabled and fictional assigned work/process contacts. Keep the fixture banner and no-real-provider limitation. Provide direct first-work/help actions, separate publisher tools, and repair the320px More target to the44CSS-pixel house minimum without overflow.

Batch35-R3, only after R1/R2 local checks: reuse P34 security commands, give their UI understandable permission/scope/name/date and impact-review language, and separate real publication from inspection/simulation. Do not rebuild lineage/custody enforcement. Then implement the original shared configuration draft/validate/preview/publish/history slice below using the same bounded editor pattern. P35 may require several CONTINUE executions; record R1/R2/R3 separately.
checks: An ordinary member and a head can locate title, owner/date and the actual permitted next action without traversing unrelated editors; nonfinancial work consistently says review not required while governed/pending/unavailable work remains distinct. Hidden case titles/counts are never exposed.

Edit then refresh/back/conflict/timeout keeps safe inputs or obtains explicit discard intent; identical retry cannot duplicate an effect, and sign-out/scope loss clears the prior account state. Verify existing security/state tests still pass.

The coherent synthetic preview supports assigned-task discovery, scoped help and sandbox practice with the real components; guest cannot browse the roster, and practice creates no task/request/FIN/outbox. Record desktop/mobile role coverage, not a human usability pass.

Plain-language named access-impact review preserves exact scope/expiry/ceilings and independently acknowledged custody. At320px the five mobile primary targets meet44px house sizing without horizontal overflow; technical proofs remain available through scoped details rather than required member knowledge.

additional_context: docs/build/ADOPTION-DELIVERY.md, docs/readiness.md, docs/tasks.md, docs/resources-onboarding.md and docs/access-administration.md for the current equivalent interfaces; P34 mutation is delivered locally, not an absent prerequisite

title: Add readable work references and build the request form editor
interface: Editor produces the same FormDefinition accepted by P20, preserving stable keys/options and routing confidential payloads correctly.
steps: Implement field/section add/edit/reorder/remove-draft, supported types, help, required conditions, options and repeatable lines with keyboard controls.
Add synthetic preview and schema validation; enforce limits and fixed operators. Reserved finance/approval values remain typed protected fields.
Publish through P35; show impact on drafts and explicit migration rather than changing submitted data. Explain why confidential fields need restricted storage/type.
checks: Renaming a label does not change stored field key/old answer meaning.
A confidential custom field cannot publish into broad ordinary JSON.
Published old form submissions remain readable under their version; unsafe condition/code and excessive schema size fail.

work: Batch36-R1 before the form editor: implement the missing member-facing references for existing tasks and deliverables, using TASK-027 and DEL-012 as default display formats, with the term separate where needed. Keep UUID primary keys/deep links and existing FIN/MCD/general request IDs unchanged. Add a reviewed migration for server-only per-term/per-kind allocation and deterministic resumable backfill, serialized with new creation and existing idempotent commands; no UUID truncation, recycled sequence or mutation of issued IDs. Extend existing authorized list/detail selectors with display references, title-first labels and Copy reference/Copy link. Reference lookup must authorize before revealing existence; exact global search remains P43.

Batch36-R2: build the original bounded form editor from useful templates with named field/section controls, readable confidentiality help and optional advanced conditions. Group longer requester forms into relevant steps with Back/Change/Review and safe in-memory input retention. Simple tasks/requests must not acquire irrelevant finance/provider/profile fields. Stable field/option keys stay internal and unchanged when labels move or rename.
checks: Concurrent creation, identical retry and interrupted/resumed backfill produce one immutable reference per record and no duplicate qualified(term,kind,sequence) reference; numbering grows past999 without truncation. Renames/revisions preserve issued refs and old UUID links; existing request refs are byte-for-byte unchanged.

Short reference never grants access: another unit/expired guest cannot resolve a hidden title/count/record by guessing a ref. Cross-term display/copy includes unambiguous term context; failed/unsaved creation is not falsely announced as issued.

A representative short requester form can be completed without keys/codes or irrelevant sections; Back/validation/conflict preserves safe fields, conditional hidden values cannot bypass server rules, and published forms remain compatible with P20/P35 and historical submissions.

additional_context: docs/build/ADOPTION-DELIVERY.md, docs/work-items.md, docs/tasks.md and the existing request-submission contract discovered under docs for stable UUIDs, current creation commands and request tracking

title: Build the bounded workflow and approval editor
interface: Workflow editor emits P22-compatible sequential stable stages, one/all eligible reviewers, revision routes and bounded conditions; publication uses P35.
steps: Implement stage ordering, reviewer/role/scope resolution, required evidence, decision routes, authorized delegates and reminder settings.
Preview synthetic cases including requester conflict and missing authority; show open cases pinned to previous versions.
Reject unbounded loops, unsafe scripts, nonexistent approvers and configurations bypassing FIN/MCD protected policy. No generic BPM product.
checks: Head can configure a service review without editing source code.
Removing a required financial/creative authority or assigning only requester as reviewer fails publication.
New version applies to new instances; an active old case continues or explicitly migrates with audited authority.

work: Use a bounded stage-list editor with useful service templates, named eligible people/roles and ordinary decision labels. Put required gate/conflict explanations at the affected stage; keep technical operators/keys in advanced details. Reuse P35 draft/impact/review/publish/history and edit-recovery behavior.

Preview the requester journey and next person/action for happy, revision, missing-reviewer and self-conflict cases; do not expose a general BPM canvas or imply that a new workflow expands the installed single-stage FIN/MCD typed adapters. Unsupported institutional mappings remain paused.
checks: A scoped head configures an ordinary sequential service using named controls and can see who handles each step and why an invalid stage is blocked; old active cases retain their pinned routing and current server authority.

Back/preview/validation and a stale-editor conflict preserve the draft; unsupported protected routing cannot publish, and ordinary members cannot enter configuration or gain reviewer authority from its labels.

title: Edit phases, semantic statuses and service routing
interface: Admin controls edit display labels/order, phase dates and service contacts while stable IDs/semantic categories remain authoritative.
steps: Add phase management and current-phase display; validate active phase selection and date order without assuming prototype phase names.
Add status-label/color/order editor with protected semantics and accessible contrast; cannot turn a pending state into an approved decision.
Add service name/description, receiving unit, primary/backup contacts, official form link, lead-time text and guest eligibility with impact validation.
checks: Renamed PRISM/status/phase does not change authority, routes or historical meaning.
Invalid phase date range or inactive required contact is reported before publish.
A status called Approved without a valid decision still fails readiness; published copy updates through versioned config.

work: Use one consistent display model for Not required, Waiting for review, Approved for this revision and Unavailable; named statuses cannot override authoritative semantics. Show active phase dates and actual permitted primary/backup help routes in member-facing process pages.

For newly configured ordinary tracking namespaces, require a unique recognizable short prefix(default2-6uppercase letters); separate it from mutable unit labels and retain old long prefixes/issued references permanently. Validate the existing allocator namespace, alias and collision rules rather than renumbering historical requests.
checks: Changing a display status/phase/service name cannot change required approvals, reference or old pinned meaning; all relevant cards agree on gate applicability without revealing private cases.

New short prefix collisions/unsafe reserved FIN-MCD namespaces are refused; old long refs and renamed-unit aliases still resolve only within current access. Missing contacts provide a concrete permitted repair route and cannot appear live-ready.

title: Implement general site Edit Mode, labels and branding
interface: Site pages use safe block catalog and label/theme config via P35; approved-logo asset separate from interface font/accent.
steps: Implement authenticated contextual Edit Mode for supported text/link/card blocks, navigation wording/order, guide copy and branding tokens.
Add draft/preview/diff/publish/revert and role-aware synthetic previews. Keep licensed logo shape/name/color protected by approved-asset selection and MCD review record.
Check contrast and focus visibility; keep Karla/calm tokens by default. No arbitrary HTML/CSS/JavaScript injection or fresh decorative redesign.
checks: Typing in Edit Mode is private until publish and rollback records a new version.
Renaming labels does not break deep links, workflow semantics or permission keys.
Unsafe block content or inaccessible token combination is rejected/warned with a concrete repair; ordinary members cannot enter editor.

work: Keep a stable small everyday navigation grouped by member task; role-only tools stay separate, and disabled optional modules have no links/setup nags. Contextual Edit Mode is visibly different from using the app; use the common P35 save/preview/publish pattern with safe unsaved-change recovery.

Allow approved wording changes with preview on ordinary member, head and guest layouts; retain deep links, first-use acronym explanations, approved identity text and access enforcement. Fix the no-space mobile text identity without inventing a licensed logo.
checks: A navigation/wording publication preserves current short refs, old deep links, restricted destinations and an obvious first-work/help route for the intended role.
Leaving/refreshing editor mode cannot silently discard or publish a draft; an ordinary member cannot enter editor mode, and disabled modules stay absent from both navigation and mandatory setup.

title: Configure widgets and layouts by role
interface: Role/unit layout config selects fixed widget IDs and supported options; each widget independently queries authorized data.
steps: Implement role layouts, responsive placement/order/size, saved operational views and preview. Provide keyboard Move Up/Down, not drag-only controls.
Offer existing task/waiting/deliverables/synergy/review/calendar/resource widgets only; optional-module widgets appear only when enabled.
Retain a required route/action path so layout cannot hide all next actions; prevent arbitrary SQL/query definition.
checks: A member cannot obtain FIN data by adding a FIN widget to a layout.
Same layout remains usable on 320px screen and with keyboard reordering.
Missing/retired widget produces a clear safe fallback and configuration validation, not a broken dashboard.

work: Provide a useful default home prioritizing next action, owner/date and blockers, with optional secondary widgets behind purposeful groups. No member must personalize a dashboard before work; do not show all widgets at equal emphasis.

Layout preview must cover a late joiner/no work, a current assignee, a head and a guest using coherent fixtures. Preserve required actions/help,320px/zoom/keyboard behavior and independently authorized widget queries.
checks: Fresh/no-work and retired-widget layouts retain a direct current contact/assigned-work path; adding/reordering widgets cannot hide all next actions or manufacture FIN/guest access.

The same representative next-action journey remains discoverable across default/custom/mobile layouts with44px controls; saved configuration does not require member setup or duplicate authoritative work.

title: Configure notification rules, schedules and preferences
interface: Rules select fixed events/audiences/channels with dedup, bounded schedule and Manila quiet hours; delivery preference does not remove required work.
steps: Add admin rules, recipient dry-run, safe templates, due/overdue reminders, digest/mute choices and channel availability.
Implement default two-days-before/due-day/daily-overdue scheduling and 20:00–08:00 quiet period as editable proposals, using tested Manila dates.
Use durable deduplication and outbox dispatch; external channels remain disabled until configured/verified in optional steps.
checks: Scheduler retry/window overlap creates no duplicate digest or reminder.
Muted external delivery does not hide the in-app pending obligation.
Recipient preview respects access; private payload cannot be inserted into external-message templates.

work: Explain each rule as event, audience, channel and time with a no-send recipient preview. Group useful updates and link directly to the permitted action; use clear saved/muted/delivery-unavailable states rather than another task queue.

Keep scheduling code/test proposals separate from live cadence activation. Existing no-schedule/no-external-message instructions remain unless separately authorized; mute and missing channels never hide the authoritative in-app obligation.
checks: A permitted recipient can identify the actual next action from a grouped in-app alert; mute/retry/quiet-hour overlap cannot duplicate obligations or obscure still-pending work.
Rule preview sends nothing and reveals no hidden recipients/payload; unconfigured channels show a useful fallback and do not generate connection nags for ordinary members.

title: Publish scoped announcements and acknowledgments
interface: Published announcement has audience, immutable revisions, pin/expiry, publisher and acknowledgments against material revision.
steps: Build draft/publish/edit/pin/expire and core/committee audience selection for authorized publishers.
Add acknowledgment and material-edit renewed acknowledgment without treating it as a legal waiver.
Wire overview/inbox and private file visibility. Guests need explicit share; resource-draft ability is not announcement publisher authority.
checks: Other committee/guest cannot enumerate unshared announcement contents or counts.
Materially edited announcement does not reuse prior acknowledgment silently.
Narrower attachment remains restricted even when announcement audience is wider.

work: Keep announcements subordinate to current work; use concise audience/publisher/expiry and a clear Read or Acknowledge action. Only material required revisions renew acknowledgment; do not turn routine announcement reading into a repeated onboarding course.
Use P35 authoring/review/unsaved-input behavior in a distinct authorized publisher area; opening an announcement must not look like accepting a task, legal waiver or financial approval.
checks: A new member can distinguish reading/acknowledgment from an assigned task/approval; material revision resets only the appropriate acknowledgment and an expired pin no longer crowds the home.
Publisher conflict preserves safe input, and a broader announcement never widens attachment or guest scope; hidden announcements reveal no content/count.

title: Implement permission-filtered keyword search
interface: search_workspace(query, filters, cursor) applies authorization before snippets/counts across operational titles/IDs, guides and allowed contacts.
steps: Add suitable PostgreSQL full-text/trigram indexes and exact term-aware tracking lookup; support renamed-unit aliases.
Build categorized accessible results, empty/error states and safe restricted-result behavior.
Exclude finance raw payload, evaluations, private profile fields and attachment extraction from global index. No external AI search.
checks: Searching a known private title/amount/contact or restricted ID reveals no existence/count/snippet.
Exact ID distinguishes terms and maps renamed unit aliases without collisions.
Typeahead/keyboard/mobile behavior works; SQL parameters and pagination cannot widen scope.

work: Add title-first search and exact short-reference lookup for current request/task/deliverable formats, qualified by term and stable namespace. Show readable result context, copy/open links and old-unit aliases; members need not know an ID to find work.
Keep categorized results/filters progressive and keyboard/mobile friendly. Treat no match, connection failure and lost permission distinctly without exposing whether a restricted match exists.
checks: Exact ref and title searches reach the same permitted record; duplicate short refs in different terms are disambiguated and renamed/old aliases never return the wrong item.
Guessing an inaccessible reference/title yields no existence/count/snippet; keyboard selection, clear search and retry preserve the intended scope/context without long-code entry.

title: Build workload, readiness and meaningful-usage reports
interface: Scoped SQL reports use documented event allowlist and Monday–Sunday Manila periods; minimal first-party events, no sensitive bodies.
steps: Implement readiness, overdue/original dates, blocked duration, queue age, handoff/approval turnaround and assigned workload with clear definitions.
Add meaningful weekly active numerator/eligible-core denominator, excluding guests/tests/bots; instrument safe work views/actions and retention for usage events.
Restrict supervisory breakdowns and exports; no public member ranking, affiliation comparison or fake utilization percentages.
checks: At 89 eligible members, at least 72 meaningful active members meets 80%; logins/bot pings alone do not.
Multi-unit users are counted once and Manila week boundary is correct.
Changing deadline does not erase original overdue history; small/private groups do not reveal protected records.

work: Separate manager reports from the everyday next-action home. Place concise metric definitions/time period/denominator beside the report; prefer actionable scoped summaries over dense default charts or rankings.
Use readable titles/refs and authorized drill-through for a manager investigation. Keep usage telemetry minimal; learnability results are actual UAT records, not a score inferred from login/activity.
checks: A scoped head can explain a representative blocked/overdue metric and open only its permitted source work; no raw payload, small-group identity or public member ranking leaks.
Zero data, stale data and unsupported filters produce an understandable safe state rather than fake percentages; operational activity is never relabeled newcomer task success.

title: Add previewed Sheets-compatible CSV import and scoped export
interface: Import preview/mapping/validation commits through authorized existing commands with stable IDs; export uses effective scope and spreadsheet-safe values.
steps: Support roster/tasks import templates, row-level error report, deduplication, dry-run and confirmation of exact mapped changes.
Do not turn role columns or imported identity fields into unreviewed privileges; sensitive financial imports use separate authorized template/reconciliation.
Export permitted operations with stable IDs and neutralize spreadsheet formula prefixes; preserve dates/UTF-8/newlines correctly. No bidirectional Sheets sync.
checks: Repeated import does not duplicate records and partial errors are reported consistently with chosen atomicity.
CSV containing =,+,-,@ formula payloads cannot execute when opened in a spreadsheet as exported user content.
Unauthorized export/import changes fail; role field cannot grant admin and unrelated private rows never appear.

work: Provide a small example CSV template, named column mapping, readable row-specific repair messages and exact before/after confirmation. Ordinary task import uses known people/refs rather than requiring UUIDs or permission codes.
Preserve old/issued short refs and UUID relationships across import/export. A resumable failed import retains mapping/input context safely and must not duplicate work or require manual numbering.
checks: A malformed/duplicate row can be repaired and retried without duplicating a task, changing its issued ref, assigning implicit authority or losing the remaining review context.
Export contains permitted title/ref/term context and safe spreadsheet values; unauthorized lookups/import mapping cannot disclose hidden roster or case details.

title: Implement privacy notice, restricted access logs and retention controls
interface: Versioned privacy notice, category retention_rules, legal_holds, auditable access/export and timed emergency grants; routine private reads use audited restricted endpoints.
steps: Build notice/optional sharing acknowledgments, custodian request intake, authorized access/correction/export handling, retention policy configuration and hold review.
Implement dry-run disposition/purge planning without running live deletion; distinguish archive from erasure, preserve necessary minimal ledger and restore replay.
Add time-bounded emergency access with reason/notification and no routine broad admin contents. Block sensitive-module activation without owner/basis/retention decisions.
checks: Legal hold prevents scheduled disposal and dry-run lists affected records/files without exposing their contents.
Admin cannot silently self-grant indefinite raw FIN/PRISM access through UI.
All normal restricted reads/exports are logged through authorized endpoints; raw sensitive payloads/tokens do not enter telemetry.

work: Give members plain-purpose privacy choices and a real permitted help/request route, separate from custodian retention/emergency tools. Optional profile data remains optional; guide/notice acknowledgment cannot become a fabricated legal waiver.

Use a guided custodian impact review for holds/disposition/emergency expiry; keep technical ledger details available separately. Simplification may not widen sensitive access or invent deferred institutional decisions.
checks: A member with blank optional affiliation/course can use essential work/help and request access/correction through the approved route; they cannot browse other requests or custodian-only raw content.
A custodian can identify category/hold/action/expiry from a safe dry run; no purge executes or indefinite self-grant arises from the review flow, and pending policy inputs stay visibly blocked.

title: Implement encrypted backup and prove identity/file recovery
interface: Backup manifest covers app data/config, schema, file bytes/hashes, identity linkage recovery, retention/purge replay and separate key custody; freshness visible to custodians.
steps: Implement documented encrypted export and verify tools' actual Auth/Storage inclusion/exclusion. Keep backups/secrets out of Git artifacts and ordinary member folders.
Add restoration into an explicitly verified isolated local/authorized recovery target; preserve stable member IDs or test verified provider re-linking.
Rehearse login, permissions, immutable decisions/files and purge replay; record actual RPO/RTO, missing prerequisites and second-custodian runbook. Do not invent a successful rehearsal.
checks: Restored user can log in to correct scope; unauthorized user cannot read recovered private files.
Manifest counts/file hashes match and expired/purged data does not silently resurrect.
Stale/failed backup appears in health; missing device/provider/key makes verification blocked, not green.

work: Provide a stepwise custodian recovery runbook with clear prerequisites, last verified backup and actionable failure/retry status. Keep encryption, hashes and full manifests in scoped operational details rather than ordinary member pages.

Have a second custodian follow the documented isolated restore sample when actual access/keys/target are available. Record observed completion and missing steps; do not replace a real rehearsal with a generated checklist.
checks: An interrupted/stale/missing backup or failed restore cannot show healthy/complete; retry is resumable and verifies counts, bytes, identity scope and purge replay.
A second custodian can locate the next recovery action and evidence without author assistance when actually observed; otherwise that human/operational result remains pending.
